# Tool reference: SimCity 3000 server (simcity3000)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_tool_docs.py from the server's tools/list; do not edit by hand -->

81 tools. Every tool takes JSON arguments as described and returns compact JSON text, except `guide` (markdown), `map_text` (the ASCII map) and `screenshot` / `map_image` (a PNG image). Failures are MCP tool errors (`isError: true`) whose text is JSON `{"error": ..., "hint": ...}`.

Kinds map to the MCP tool annotations each tool carries:

| kind | readOnlyHint | destructiveHint | idempotentHint | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| read | True | False | True | reads the game, changes nothing |
| observe | True | False | False | reads; has a 'since last call' cursor |
| set | False | False | True | sets a value (idempotent) |
| act | False | False | False | acts in the game |
| destructive | False | True | False | can discard or destroy something (unsaved city, buildings, a deal, a file, the game process) |

All tools have openWorldHint false (they act on the local game only).

## Server instructions

Sent to the client at initialization:

> Plays a live SimCity 3000 Unlimited game: everything is read from the game's memory and every action goes through the game's own code (normal costs and rules). Call guide() for the full how-to. Start with game_launch, then load_city / new_city, or start_trial(name, seed) for a reproducible experiment. Observe with metrics, city_status, get_budget, population_details, zone_summary, map_text, tile_info; act with build, place_building, set_tax, set_ordinance...; run time with advance_time (exact game days; it returns early with remaining_days after max_seconds or when the game asks something: dialog_status / close_dialog). Tiles are (x, y) as map_text shows them. Errors come back as tool errors with JSON {error, hint}.

## guide

*read*

How to use this server (markdown text): starting a game, map coordinates, building, time, dialogs and petitions, money, which tool answers which question, reproducible experiments, errors and the rules of play. Read it once before playing.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic` | string | `''` | A section title or part of it (e.g. "time", "experiments"); empty for the whole guide. |

## game_launch

*set*

Start SimCity 3000 Unlimited (windowed 1024x768, intro skipped) and attach to it, or attach to the copy that is already running; waits for the main menu. Call this first, then load_city, new_city, load_scenario or start_trial.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reload_bridge` | boolean | `false` | Development only: re-inject a freshly built bridge DLL into the running game. Leave false. |

## game_status

*read*

Whether the game runs, which screen it shows (main menu, city, terrain editor), the city basics (name, date, funds, paused, speed) and any open game dialog. Cheap; safe to call at any time.

No parameters.

## new_city

*destructive*

Start a new city through the game's New City screens. The current city is discarded without saving (save_city first if it matters). The simulation starts paused in the chosen year.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `'New City'` | City name. |
| `mayor` | string | `'Mayor'` | Mayor name. |
| `difficulty` | string | `'easy'` | easy ($50,000 to start) \| medium ($20,000) \| hard ($10,000, as a loan). |
| `start_year` | integer | `1900` | 1900 \| 1950 \| 2000. |
| `size` | string | `'large'` | Map size: miniature (64x64 tiles) \| small (128x128) \| medium (192x192) \| large (256x256). |
| `disasters` | boolean | `false` | Enable random disasters. |
| `auto_budget` | boolean | `false` | Enable the game's Auto Budget (otherwise the Budget window opens every 1 January). |
| `regenerate_terrain` | integer | `0` | Re-roll the random terrain this many extra times. |
| `hills` | integer or null | `null` | Terrain hills 0-100; omit to keep the game's default. |
| `water` | integer or null | `null` | Terrain water 0-100; omit to keep the default. |
| `trees` | integer or null | `null` | Terrain trees 0-100; omit to keep the default. |
| `feature` | string or null | `null` | none \| lake \| river_nw_se \| river_sw_ne \| mountain; omit to keep the default. |
| `coasts` | array of string or null | `null` | Map edges with sea, any of NW (the y=0 edge), NE (x=0), SE (y=max), SW (x=max); [] for none; omit to keep the default. |
| `accept_terrain` | boolean | `true` | true starts the city at once; false stays in the terrain editor (generate_terrain, edit_terrain, then finish_map_editor). |

## generate_terrain

*act*

Terrain editor only (after new_city(accept_terrain=false) or loading a terrain): set the terrain parameters and press Re-Generate. Returns the settings as the editor shows them.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hills` | integer or null | `null` | 0-100; omit to keep. |
| `water` | integer or null | `null` | 0-100; omit to keep. |
| `trees` | integer or null | `null` | 0-100; omit to keep. |
| `feature` | string or null | `null` | none \| lake \| river_nw_se \| river_sw_ne \| mountain; omit to keep. |
| `coasts` | array of string or null | `null` | Any of NW (the y=0 edge), NE (x=0), SE (y=max), SW (x=max); [] for none; omit to keep. |

## edit_terrain

*act*

Terrain editor only: use one of the editor's free tools, dragging from tile (x, y) to (x2, y2). In a running city use build with raise_terrain / lower_terrain / level_terrain / trees / water instead (those cost money).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | string | required | raise \| lower \| level \| trees \| water \| bulldoze. |
| `x` | integer | required | Start tile x. |
| `y` | integer | required | Start tile y. |
| `x2` | integer or null | `null` | End tile x; omit for a single tile. |
| `y2` | integer or null | `null` | End tile y; omit for a single tile. |

## finish_map_editor

*act*

Terrain editor only: accept the terrain and start the city (paused).

No parameters.

## list_cities

*read*

Files the game can load from its Cities folder (saved cities, starter towns, real-city terrains, scenarios), each with the name and kind to pass to load_city or start_trial.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string or null | `null` | Only this kind: city \| starter_town \| terrain \| scenario; omit for all. |

## load_city

*destructive*

Load a file the way the game's Load menu does; the current city is discarded without saving. kind city loads a saved city (paused). starter_town and terrain start a new city on that map with the New City Options below; a terrain then opens the terrain editor (generate_terrain / edit_terrain / finish_map_editor). For reproducible experiments use start_trial instead.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | File name as list_cities shows it (no extension), e.g. "Berlin, Germany". |
| `kind` | string | `'city'` | city \| starter_town \| terrain \| scenario (scenarios are better started with load_scenario). |
| `city_name` | string | `''` | Name for the new city (starter_town / terrain only). |
| `mayor` | string | `''` | Mayor name (starter_town / terrain only). |
| `difficulty` | string | `'easy'` | easy \| medium \| hard (starter_town / terrain only). |
| `disasters` | boolean | `false` | Enable random disasters (starter_town / terrain only). |
| `auto_budget` | boolean | `false` | Enable Auto Budget (starter_town / terrain only). |

## start_trial

*destructive*

Start a reproducible experiment: quit and restart the game (a fresh process, about 12 s), make all of its randomness follow `seed`, then load the file as load_city does. The same seed, the same actions and the same advance_time calls give exactly the same city; different seeds give independent trials of one strategy. (Plain load_city is not reproducible: the game seeds its random numbers from the clock and keeps some traffic state across loads.)

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | File name as list_cities shows it. |
| `seed` | integer | required | Any integer; the same seed reproduces the same run. |
| `kind` | string | `'city'` | city \| starter_town \| terrain \| scenario (as load_city). |

## load_scenario

*destructive*

Start one of the game's scenarios; the current city is discarded. Returns the briefing and the goals (scenario_status tracks them). Some scenarios cannot be paused or sped up.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Scenario name as list_cities(kind="scenario") shows it. |

## scenario_status

*read*

The running scenario: name, description, goals with met / not met, months elapsed and, once it has ended, the final rank (1 is best) and result text. {"scenario": false} outside scenarios.

No parameters.

## save_city

*destructive*

Save the current city as Cities/<name>.sc3 through the game's Save As dialog. An existing file is replaced only with overwrite=true; the game's own shipped cities are never overwritten.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | File name without extension. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | `false` | Replace an existing file of that name. |

## rename_city

*set*

Rename the city and/or its mayor (the game's City Options window).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string or null | `null` | New city name; omit to keep. |
| `mayor` | string or null | `null` | New mayor name; omit to keep. |

## set_auto_budget

*set*

Turn the game's Auto Budget option on or off. With it off the game opens the Budget window every 1 January (set_auto_mode("info") closes it and carries on).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | required | true = on. |

## quit_game

*destructive*

Quit SimCity 3000 without saving. game_launch starts it again.

No parameters.

## city_status

*read*

The city at a glance: name, mayor, date, funds, population, commercial and industrial jobs, RCI demand (-1..1 per zone), power and water capacity and use, buildings without power / water, average land value and crime, average air / water / garbage pollution, the disasters and auto-budget options, whether a disaster is running, paused, speed and map size. Cheap; call it often.

No parameters.

## metrics

*read*

One flat snapshot of the numbers that measure how well the city runs, for logging every step of an experiment: date, population, funds, yearly income / expense estimates and their difference, debt, tax rates, RCI demand, jobs, unemployment %, education (EQ), life expectancy, power and water use vs capacity, unserved buildings, land value, crime, air / water pollution, garbage produced vs handled, school / college / hospital use vs capacity and (traffic=true) the share of road tiles with heavy or congested traffic. advance_time(record=...) returns a series of these.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `traffic` | boolean | `true` | Include the road congestion share (scans the traffic layer). |

## map_text

*read*

Exact ASCII map of a region, one character per tile (rows = y, columns = x, with axis labels and a legend): the cheapest way to see the layout without images.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer` | string | `'auto'` | auto (buildings over zones over terrain) \| terrain \| zones \| buildings \| a data layer: landvalue, crime, police, fire, air, water_pollution, radiation, garbage, power, water, pipes, traffic, aura, flammability, density. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | Left tile x. |
| `y0` | integer | `0` | Top tile y. |
| `x1` | integer or null | `null` | Right tile x, inclusive; omit for the map edge. |
| `y1` | integer or null | `null` | Bottom tile y, inclusive; omit for the map edge. |
| `step` | integer | `1` | Show every step-th tile (step > 1 gives an overview of a large map). |

## map_data

*read*

Raw numbers of one data layer for a region, for analysis: rows[i][j] is the value at tile (x0 + j*step, y0 + i*step). At most 16,384 values per call (use step or a smaller region). tile_info gives the game's labels.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer` | string | required | landvalue \| crime \| police \| fire \| air \| water_pollution \| radiation \| garbage \| power \| water \| pipes \| traffic \| aura \| flammability \| density. |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | Left tile x. |
| `y0` | integer | `0` | Top tile y. |
| `x1` | integer or null | `null` | Right tile x, inclusive; omit for the map edge. |
| `y1` | integer or null | `null` | Bottom tile y, inclusive; omit for the map edge. |
| `step` | integer | `1` | Sample every step-th tile. |

## layer_stats

*read*

Distribution of a data layer over a set of tiles: count, mean, min / percentiles / max, the game's labels (e.g. traffic None / Light / Medium / Heavy / Congested) and the share of tiles at or above each threshold. Example: police coverage on residential tiles with thresholds [50, 100].

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer` | string | required | A data layer, as map_data. |
| `where` | string | `'all'` | Which tiles: all \| zoned \| residential \| commercial \| industrial \| a zone name (res_dense, landfill...) \| roads \| highways \| rail \| subways \| stations \| network. |
| `thresholds` | array of integer or null | `null` | Values t for which to report the share of tiles with value >= t. |

## map_image

*read*

Top-down colour picture of the whole map (one tile = scale pixels), optionally tinted by a data layer. Only useful to clients that can view images; map_text and map_data carry the same information as text.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scale` | integer | `3` | Pixels per tile. |
| `overlay` | string or null | `null` | A data layer to tint the map with (as map_data); omit for none. |

## tile_info

*read*

Everything at one tile: corner altitudes and water, zone, occupants (category, name, footprint) and every data layer (land value, crime, police, fire, pollution, radiation, garbage, power, water, pipes, traffic, aura, flammability) with the game's labels.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Tile x, 0 .. map width - 1 (city_status map_size). |
| `y` | integer | required | Tile y, 0 .. map height - 1. |

## buildings

*read*

List occupants (buildings and network pieces) with category, name and footprint rect [x0, y0, x1, y1]. With details=true: buildings only, each with state, residents / jobs, power and water service, land value and its class data (as building_info).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name_filter` | string or null | `null` | Only names containing this text, e.g. "Plant", "Road", "Res"; omit for all. |
| `x0` | integer | `-1` | Region left tile x (-1 with the others = whole map). |
| `y0` | integer | `-1` | Region top tile y. |
| `x1` | integer | `-1` | Region right tile x. |
| `y1` | integer | `-1` | Region bottom tile y. |
| `include_trees` | boolean | `false` | Include trees (there can be tens of thousands). |
| `limit` | integer | `300` | Maximum number of entries returned. |
| `details` | boolean | `false` | Buildings only, with per-building data. |

## building_info

*read*

Everything the game knows about the building covering tile (x, y): name, type, zone / density / wealth, state (working, abandoned, under construction, destroyed...), residents or jobs, powered, watered, land value; power plants: fuel, output, capacity, age, life span; water buildings: source, capacity, use, intake, pipe connection; police / fire: coverage radius and cost; jails: inmates; stations: passengers per day; garbage, recycling and treatment buildings: capacity and use; every data layer at that tile; and (game_query) the lines of the game's own Query window for it (e.g. crimes and arrests per month, performance rating, attendance, grades).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Any tile x of the building. |
| `y` | integer | required | Any tile y of the building. |
| `game_query` | boolean | `true` | Also run the game's Query tool on it and include its lines (about a second). |

## zone_summary

*read*

City-wide building totals: buildings by state, residents and jobs; per zone / density / wealth (or industry type) the number of buildings, working, abandoned, residents and jobs; and per zone type the zoned tiles and how many of them are still undeveloped.

No parameters.

## population_details

*read*

Demographics and services, city-wide: population by age and, per age group, education (EQ) and life expectancy (the Population window's three pages), children / workforce / seniors, education (EQ) and life expectancy, jobs and unemployment, schools / colleges / hospitals (users, capacity, staff, grade, strikes), library and museum capacity, garbage flows and landfill fullness, average pollution.

No parameters.

## building_counts

*read*

Number of occupants per category name (trees, road pieces, houses, plants...), most common first.

No parameters.

## screenshot

*read*

PNG of the game window's client area (1024x768), only for clients that can view images: every number the other tools return is read from memory, not from pictures. Full-size pixel coordinates are what ui_click expects.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scale` | number | `0.75` | Shrink factor for the returned picture (coordinates stay full-size). |
| `x0` | integer | `0` | Crop left pixel. |
| `y0` | integer | `0` | Crop top pixel. |
| `x1` | integer or null | `null` | Crop right pixel; omit for the edge. |
| `y1` | integer or null | `null` | Crop bottom pixel; omit for the edge. |

## center_view

*set*

Centre the game's camera on tile (x, y). Only changes what the screen and screenshots show.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Tile x. |
| `y` | integer | required | Tile y. |
| `zoom` | integer or null | `null` | 0 (farthest) .. 4 (closest); omit to keep. |

## set_view

*set*

The game window's camera and display layers, as its rotate / zoom buttons and Layer Views panel set them (only what the screen and screenshots show). Returns the view: centre tile, zoom, rotation, data view, layers. Call it without arguments to read the view.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rotation` | integer or null | `null` | 0..3 (quarter turns); omit to keep. |
| `zoom` | integer or null | `null` | 0 (farthest) .. 4 (closest); omit to keep. |
| `data_view` | string or null | `null` | normal \| subways \| pipes (the underground views) \| aura \| crime \| power \| flammability \| landvalue \| pollution \| traffic \| density (the game's data overlays); omit to keep. |
| `zones` | boolean or null | `null` | Show zone colours. |
| `transport` | boolean or null | `null` | Show roads, rail and other transport. |
| `power_lines` | boolean or null | `null` | Show power lines. |
| `trees` | boolean or null | `null` | Show trees. |
| `zoned_buildings` | boolean or null | `null` | Show buildings on zones. |
| `other_buildings` | boolean or null | `null` | Show all other buildings. |
| `grid` | boolean or null | `null` | Show the terrain grid (the G key). |

## find_empty_area

*read*

Find places to build: up to `limit` non-overlapping rectangles of width x height tiles with nothing built (trees are fine), no zoning, no water and (flat=true) level ground, nearest to (near_x, near_y). Returns their top-left and bottom-right tiles.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | integer | required | Width in tiles (along x). |
| `height` | integer | required | Height in tiles (along y). |
| `near_x` | integer or null | `null` | Search around this tile x; omit for the map centre. |
| `near_y` | integer or null | `null` | Search around this tile y; omit for the map centre. |
| `flat` | boolean | `true` | Require level ground (most buildings need it). |
| `limit` | integer | `5` | Maximum number of areas returned. |

## tool_catalog

*read*

The build tools for build / build_many (name, kind, description) and the buildings of the power, water and garbage pickers. kind line: drag from (x, y) to (x2, y2); area: the rectangle (x, y)..(x2, y2); click: one tile (buildings are placed by their top-left tile).

No parameters.

## build

*act*

Use one of the game's build tools (tool_catalog) at the game's normal cost: line tools (road, rail, power_line, pipe...) from (x, y) to (x2, y2); area tools (zones, dezone, landfill...) over the rectangle; click tools (stations, services, parks, trees...) at (x, y) or at every tile of the rectangle. Returns the cost charged (0 = the game refused) and what changed, read back from memory. If the game asks a question (e.g. whether to build a bridge) the result says so: answer with close_dialog.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | string | required | Tool name from tool_catalog, e.g. road, res_light, power_line, police_station. |
| `x` | integer | required | Start tile x (a building's top-left tile). |
| `y` | integer | required | Start tile y. |
| `x2` | integer or null | `null` | End tile x; omit for one tile. |
| `y2` | integer or null | `null` | End tile y; omit for one tile. |

## bulldoze

*destructive*

Demolish everything in the rectangle (x, y)..(x2, y2) with the game's bulldozer (normal demolition cost) and report what was removed.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Corner tile x. |
| `y` | integer | required | Corner tile y. |
| `x2` | integer or null | `null` | Opposite corner tile x; omit for one tile. |
| `y2` | integer or null | `null` | Opposite corner tile y; omit for one tile. |

## transit

*read*

Transportation overview: stations per mode (bus, rail, subway, subway-rail) with total and busiest passengers per day (as the game's Query computes them), the transit strike state and funding, the airport (air traffic, on-time flights) and seaport (port traffic) as their Query windows show them, fares income (year to date and by month) and road / highway / rail traffic distributions with the game's None..Congested labels.

No parameters.

## rewards

*read*

Reward and business-deal buildings: what each needs (population, year, an extra condition such as EQ, life expectancy, parks, funds or airport size, from the game's City Planner table), the city's current values, whether the conditions are met, how many are built and whether the game's Rewards picker offers it now. Unlocked rewards are placed with place_building(..., picker="reward"); many are first offered as a petition (answer_petition).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check_picker` | boolean | `true` | Also open the game's Rewards picker to confirm what it offers now. |

## building_options

*read*

What one of the game's building pickers offers right now (availability by year, technology and earned rewards is the game's own).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `picker` | string | required | power \| water \| garbage \| landmark \| reward. |

## place_building

*act*

Place a building from one of the game's pickers (power plants, water buildings, garbage buildings, landmarks, rewards) by name with its top-left tile at (x, y), at the game's normal cost. The picker is opened and the building chosen there, so only what the game offers now can be placed (building_options).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Building name as building_options lists it, e.g. "Coal Power Plant". |
| `x` | integer | required | Top-left tile x. |
| `y` | integer | required | Top-left tile y. |
| `picker` | string or null | `null` | power \| water \| garbage \| landmark \| reward; omit to guess from the name. |

## build_many

*act*

Run several build / place actions in order, stopping at the first error or game question. Each action is an object: {"tool": "road", "x": 10, "y": 5, "x2": 30, "y2": 5} (as build) or {"building": "Coal Power Plant", "x": 40, "y": 40, "picker": "power"} (as place_building). Returns each result and the total cost.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | array of object | required | List of action objects as described above. |

## get_budget

*read*

Funds; tax rate, max and income per zone; department funding % and costs; yearly income / expense (to date and estimated); bonds (principal, total due, remaining, monthly payment) and debt; and the other ledgers (transit fares, neighbor and business deals, ordinance income / expense, other income) year to date and by calendar month (months after the current one still hold last year's amounts). income_ytd = taxes + all income ledgers; expense_ytd = departments + ordinance and deal expenses + bond payments.

No parameters.

## set_tax

*set*

Set a zone's property tax rate (as the Budget window's slider does).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zone` | string | required | residential \| commercial \| industrial. |
| `rate` | integer | required | Percent, 0 .. the zone's max (get_budget shows it). |

## set_department_funding

*set*

Set a department's funding level (as the Budget window does).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `department` | string | required | police \| fire \| health \| education \| roads \| transit. |
| `percent` | integer | required | 0 .. 200 (100 = full funding). |

## ordinances

*read*

All ordinances: enacted and available flags, the monthly amount each would bring (+ income) or cost (-) at the city's current size (as the Ordinances window estimates it; the actual amount for enacted ones), and the monthly totals of the enacted ones.

No parameters.

## set_ordinance

*set*

Enact or repeal an ordinance (it must be available; see ordinances).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | required | Ordinance name as ordinances lists it. |
| `enabled` | boolean | required | true = enact, false = repeal. |

## issue_bond

*act*

Take out a bond (loan). The game rounds the amount down to a multiple of $5,000 and allows at most $25,000 per bond, 10 bonds and $250,000 outstanding. It is repaid monthly over 10 years (1.2 x the principal in total) and the game has no early repayment.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer | required | Dollars. |

## petitions

*read*

Pending petitions and proposals (neighbor and business deals arrive this way): id, heading, who asks and the two answers (button1 = accept, button2 = reject; none = informational). Answer with answer_petition.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | boolean | `false` | Also include the message, the advisor's advice and the reactions. |
| `ids` | array of integer or null | `null` | Only these petition ids. |

## graphs

*read*

History of the city's graphs as the game's Graphs window has them (Residents, Education, Health, Land Value, Crime, Approval Rating, Funds, City Size, Nat'l Pop, Commerce, Industry, Unemployment, Pollution, Traffic), in the graphs' own units, newest first.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `span` | string | `'months'` | months (last 12) \| years (last 10) \| decades (last 10). |
| `names` | array of string or null | `null` | Only graphs whose name contains one of these texts. |

## news

*read*

The news ticker's current headlines by category (status, news, petitions, advisors...). game_events returns only what is new since its last call.

No parameters.

## neighbors

*read*

The four neighbor cities: name, mayor, population, the map edge each borders (and its quadrant on the game's Neighbors Map), the connections built to it (road, rail, highway, pipes, power lines, subway: a connection is what makes deals possible) and the deals with it.

No parameters.

## deals

*read*

Every neighbor deal in force (type, neighbor, monthly amount, rate, quantity, minimum, cancellation penalty, months running), proposals waiting for an answer (they arrive as petitions: answer_petition), the business-deal offers (casino, prison, gigamall, toxic waste plant; accepted ones become placeable rewards) and penalties due at the next month end. Types: buy_power, sell_power, buy_water, sell_water, export_garbage (we pay), import_garbage (they pay).

No parameters.

## cancel_deal

*destructive*

Cancel the neighbor deal of this type (see deals), as "Cancel Deal" in its terms window does. The game charges the deal's cancellation penalty at month end unless it has run 60 months.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deal_type` | string | required | buy_power \| sell_power \| buy_water \| sell_water \| export_garbage \| import_garbage. |

## discuss_deal

*act*

Open the terms of the current deal with a neighbor (the Neighbors Map's Discuss Deal button). The game shows the exact terms (quantity, price, termination fee) with the options "Keep Deal", "Cancel Deal" and "Impact Analysis": answer with close_dialog(<option>), then close_dialog("close") until dialog_status is null.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `neighbor` | string | required | Neighbor name, or its quadrant NE \| NW \| SW \| SE (see neighbors). |

## advisors

*read*

What each of the seven advisors currently says, as their panels show it (utilities, budget, city_planner, environment, health_education, public_safety, transportation), with each advisor's mood as the game computes it (1 = good news .. 5 = crisis).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | boolean | `false` | Include the messages, not only the headings. |
| `advisor` | string or null | `null` | Only this advisor. |

## answer_petition

*act*

Accept or reject a pending petition (as the meeting window's buttons do).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `petition_id` | integer | required | Id from petitions. |
| `accept` | boolean | required | true = button1 (accept), false = button2 (reject). |

## game_events

*observe*

What the game announced since the previous call (news, alerts, petitions, advisor notes from the ticker), oldest first, plus any open game dialog.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `all_recent` | boolean | `false` | Return everything the ticker still holds instead of only what is new. |

## set_auto_mode

*set*

Choose what advance_time and run_realtime do when the game opens a window. "off": stop at every window (default). "info": close windows that only inform (the year-end Budget window when Auto Budget is off, scenario notes, advisor notes, tips) and keep going, stopping only at real decisions (questions, scenario results). Windows closed this way are listed in the result's "auto_closed".

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `'info'` | off \| info. |

## advance_time

*act*

Run the simulation exactly this long, one game day at a time as fast as the engine can, then leave it paused. Months and years follow the calendar (1 March + 1 month = 1 April); days are added after them. Stops early when the game opens a window (see set_auto_mode, dialog_status) or after max_seconds of real time: the result then has "stopped_early" and "remaining_days" (advance_time(days=remaining_days) continues; the outcome is the same as one call). Returns the new date, the period's events, population, demand and funds.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | `0` | Days to run. |
| `months` | integer | `0` | Calendar months to run. |
| `years` | integer | `0` | Calendar years to run. |
| `record` | string | `''` | Also return a metrics snapshot (without traffic) at every boundary and at the end, as "series": day \| week \| month (1st of each month) \| year (1 January); empty for none. |
| `max_seconds` | number | `50.0` | Return after about this much real time even if not done, to stay within client tool timeouts (0 = no limit). A large city runs about 60 game days per second, a small one several hundred. |

## run_realtime

*act*

Let the game run in real time at a speed for up to `seconds`, then pause. Stops early as soon as the game opens a dialog (returned; answer with close_dialog). Not reproducible; prefer advance_time for experiments.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | integer | `2` | 1 (turtle) \| 2 (llama) \| 3 (cheetah) \| 4 (african swallow, the fastest). |
| `seconds` | number | `10.0` | Real seconds to run (max 600; keep it below your client's tool timeout). |

## set_paused

*set*

Pause or unpause the simulation for real-time play (advance_time does not need it). Scenarios that cannot be paused refuse.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paused` | boolean | required | true = pause. |

## set_speed

*set*

Simulation speed for real-time play. Some scenarios fix the speed.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed` | integer | required | 1 (turtle) \| 2 (llama) \| 3 (cheetah) \| 4 (african swallow, the fastest). |

## set_disasters

*set*

Enable or disable random disasters (the New City option).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | required | true = random disasters can happen. |

## trigger_disaster

*destructive*

Start a disaster now; the game picks the place. The game switches to disaster mode: the calendar stops and the game runs in real time until it is over (use disasters, run_realtime, dispatch, news).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | fire \| tornado \| earthquake \| riot \| ufo \| toxic_cloud \| whirlpool \| locusts \| space_debris. |

## preferences

*read*

The game's Preferences (read from memory, no window): traffic and pedestrians drawn at how many zoom levels, other animations, auto go to disasters, tips at startup, music / sound effects / ambient sound on-off and volumes (percent), 3D sound, which songs are in the music rotation, and the New City defaults. They change only what is drawn and heard (measured: no effect on simulation speed). Change them with set_preferences.

No parameters.

## set_preferences

*set*

Change the game's Preferences through its own Preferences window (the options are set as a player sets them, then OK; the game applies and saves them). Only the given options change; the result is read back from memory. Screen resolution is not offered (game_launch fixes the window at 1024x768).

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `traffic_visible` | integer or null | `null` | Draw traffic at the closest N zoom levels: 0 (off) .. 3. |
| `sims_visible` | integer or null | `null` | Draw pedestrians at the closest N zoom levels: 0 (off) .. 2. |
| `other_animations` | boolean or null | `null` | Other animations on / off. |
| `auto_go_to_disasters` | boolean or null | `null` | Move the camera to each new disaster. |
| `show_tips_at_startup` | boolean or null | `null` | Show the tip of the day when the game starts. |
| `music` | boolean or null | `null` | Music on / off. |
| `music_volume` | integer or null | `null` | Music volume, percent 0-100. |
| `sound_effects` | boolean or null | `null` | Sound effects on / off. |
| `sound_effects_volume` | integer or null | `null` | Sound effects volume, percent 0-100. |
| `ambient_sound` | boolean or null | `null` | Ambient sound on / off. |
| `ambient_volume` | integer or null | `null` | Ambient sound volume, percent 0-100. |
| `sound_3d` | boolean or null | `null` | Enable 3D sounds. |
| `music_tracks` | object or null | `null` | Songs to put in or take out of the music rotation, by name: {"Night Life": false, ...} (preferences lists the 17 songs). |

## query

*read*

Use the game's own Query tool on a tile and return everything its Query window shows: the title (building or terrain name) and every line with its label and value (e.g. for a fire station: elevation, powered, watered, number of fires and calls per month, performance rating, funding cost; for homes, shops, factories, plants, services, stations, ports and land the game's own lines). The window is closed again; nothing changes.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Tile x. |
| `y` | integer | required | Tile y. |

## city_options

*read*

The City Options of the current city: name, mayor, description, landscape style, tree style, building style (the game's look: e.g. European or Asian buildings), disasters and auto budget, how many user-made (Building Architect) buildings are available, and the possible style choices.

No parameters.

## set_city_options

*set*

Change the city's look and description as the City Options window does (the game re-skins the city at once; the styles are cosmetic and saved with the city). Names, disasters and auto budget: rename_city, set_disasters, set_auto_budget.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `landscape` | string or null | `null` | temperate \| winter \| desert \| dry \| tropical. |
| `trees` | string or null | `null` | mixed \| desert \| deciduous \| palms \| conifers. |
| `buildings` | string or null | `null` | north_american \| european \| asian. |
| `description` | string or null | `null` | The city's description text. |

## building_replacements

*read*

The Building Replacement Manager's data: the user-made buildings (made with the Building Architect: name, architect, size), which default buildings are currently shown as a user-made one, and (list_replaceable) the default buildings that can be replaced (id, name, size, category, current replacement). Replacements are cosmetic: same building, different look and name.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_replaceable` | boolean | `false` | Also list the replaceable default buildings (338 in all; filter with size / category). |
| `size` | integer or null | `null` | Only replaceable buildings of this footprint (1..4 tiles a side). |
| `category` | string or null | `null` | Only this category: residential \| commercial \| industrial \| rewards \| other. |

## replace_building

*set*

Show a default building as one of the user-made buildings, as the Building Replacement Manager does (Replace, then OK): every existing building of that kind changes its look and name at once; the choice is saved with the city. An empty user_building reverts it to the game's own building.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `building` | string | required | The default building's name or id (building_replacements(list_replaceable=True)). |
| `user_building` | string | `''` | The user-made building's name (same size); empty to revert. |

## reset_building_replacements

*destructive*

Clear every building replacement (the manager's Clear Set), or import the replacements saved with another city (its Import Set from Selected City). Returns the replacements now in force.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `import_from_city` | string | `''` | A saved city's name (list_cities); empty to clear all replacements instead. |
| `merge` | boolean | `true` | With import_from_city: add to the current replacements (true) or replace them (false). |

## take_snapshot

*act*

Take a snapshot with the game's own Take Snapshot (a JPG of the middle of the city view, saved by the game in its Albums folder, as in the game's Photo Album). Position the view first with center_view / set_view. Returns the file's path. Works even while the game window is not presenting on screen.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | string | `'medium'` | small \| medium \| large (640x480 is medium on a 1024x768 window: small 480x360, large 800x600). |

## snapshots

*read*

The snapshots in the game's Albums folder (the Photo Album): album, file name, path, size, time.

No parameters.

## disasters

*read*

Disasters in progress, from the game's disaster manager: whether the game is in disaster mode (calendar stopped, real time only), each active disaster instance (one per burning building, riot, swarm...) with its kind, tile, buildings destroyed and damage in $, the ones still in their warning phase, whether an early warning is on and the damage the game will partly refund when the disaster ends.

No parameters.

## dispatch

*act*

Send emergency units to tile (x, y) during a disaster, or issue an early warning.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | police \| fire \| military \| early_warning. |
| `x` | integer | required | Tile x. |
| `y` | integer | required | Tile y. |

## dialog_status

*read*

The game's open modal window, or null: kind, rect, title, text, fields and button labels. While one is open the simulation is held; answer it with close_dialog.

No parameters.

## close_dialog

*act*

Answer the open game dialog by pressing one of its buttons. If a build was waiting on this dialog it completes and its cost is returned.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `button` | string | `'ok'` | A button label as dialog_status lists it (e.g. "Yes"), or a standard result: ok \| cancel \| yes \| no \| close (closes any game window, e.g. the Neighbors Map, via its X button). |

## ui_click

*destructive*

Low-level: click the game window at client pixel (x, y) (full-size screenshot coordinates). For screens without a dedicated tool; it can press anything, so prefer the dedicated tools.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | integer | required | Pixel x, 0..1023. |
| `y` | integer | required | Pixel y, 0..767. |
| `button` | string | `'left'` | left \| right. |
| `wait_ms` | integer | `400` | Milliseconds to wait afterwards for the game to react. |

## ui_drag

*destructive*

Low-level: press the left mouse button at pixel (x1, y1), move to (x2, y2) and release.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x1` | integer | required | Start pixel x. |
| `y1` | integer | required | Start pixel y. |
| `x2` | integer | required | End pixel x. |
| `y2` | integer | required | End pixel y. |
| `wait_ms` | integer | `400` | Milliseconds to wait afterwards for the game to react. |

## ui_key

*destructive*

Low-level: press a key in the game window.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | required | A character, or esc \| enter \| space \| tab \| backspace \| delete \| home \| end \| pageup \| pagedown \| left \| up \| right \| down \| f1..f12 \| plus \| minus. |
| `shift` | boolean | `false` | Hold Shift. |
| `ctrl` | boolean | `false` | Hold Ctrl. |
| `alt` | boolean | `false` | Hold Alt. |

## ui_type

*act*

Low-level: type text into the focused game text field.

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | required | The text to type. |
